companyDossiers.name: PINS Medical

origin.detail: Founded in 2008. The primary university record links its DBS work to Luming Li’s Tsinghua team and clinical hospital partners. It documents co-development, rather than a simple sole-inventor story.

precursor.detail: The program combined electronics, hermetic packaging, leads, software and clinical neurosurgery; its first reported human DBS implantation occurred in November 2009.

companyChanges.detail: PINS took this system into commercial DBS and expanded to VNS, spinal-cord and sacral stimulation. Current company descriptions include sensing and adaptive control, whose status must be checked product by product.

milestones.detail: PINS dates its inception to 2008.

milestones.detail: University and company describe domestic DBS registration.

milestones.title: CE certification reported
milestones.detail: Tsinghua reports CE certification for the system family and subsequent overseas implants.

limits: A specific executed university technology-license agreement and complete personal founding team were not verified.
Do not collapse 2012 national-laboratory establishment and the company’s 2016 research-center date; the institution/date relationship remains unresolved.
Electrode contacts, pulse-generator channels and recorded neuron counts are different metrics.

companyDossiers.name: SceneRay

origin.detail: Yihua Ning’s official conference biography dates his founding of SceneRay to 2011 and identifies training at Shanghai Medical College. His earlier career spans medical-device engineering and management.

precursor.detail: The documented technical base is implantable DBS. The founder’s research presentation describes a dual-target NAc–ALIC stimulation program for opioid addiction.

companyChanges.detail: SceneRay’s Aaxon product history adds rechargeable designs and an eight-contact generation; Neurestora develops psychiatric indications. These changes concern stimulation architecture and use, not evidence of growing neural-recording bandwidth.

companyDossiers.name: Nurotron

origin.detail: Nurotron was established in 2006 with Hangzhou and California operations. UCI identifies Fan-Gang Zeng as a co-founder and reports that the founders worked with its technology office on commercialization.

precursor.detail: Zeng’s auditory research included sound-processing algorithms. The original device report explains cochlear stimulation hardware and technical verification, with collaborators from UCI, UCSF, UCLA, Chinese institutions and the company.

companyChanges.detail: The company translated that work into manufactured cochlear implant and external speech-processor systems. Its broader portfolio descriptions mention retinal and other stimulation directions, whose status should be kept separate from the established cochlear product.

limits: Cochlear electrodes stimulate the auditory nerve; their count is not directly comparable to intracortical BCI recording channels.

companyDossiers.name: Genlight Neurotech

origin.detail: Official history dates Genlight’s establishment to Hangzhou in 2020. A direct organizer report of a company visit names Peng Cao as founder and describes his return from France.

precursor.detail: A named founding laboratory or licensed precursor was not established. The company documents a 2021 acquisition of Hangzhou Nuowei and subsequent ZJUT training and R&D collaborations.

companyChanges.detail: The company develops distinct platforms: Epilcure couples intracranial EEG sensing to responsive stimulation; LaserRO uses MR monitoring for laser ablation. The shared neurosurgical setting does not make these the same interface technology.

companyDossiers.name: MicroPort NeuroTech / NeuroScientific

origin.detail: Founded in 2012 within a corporate medical-device lineage; parent filings document the 2022 separate listing. Its mature business is neurovascular intervention, rather than a university-origin cortical electrode platform.

precursor.detail: The company annual report identifies braiding/coiling, stent processing, balloons and catheters as established design/manufacturing capabilities. These provide an explicit engineering base for later BCI exploration.

companyChanges.detail: Its new BCI direction adds an internal research institute and a 2026 OYMotion collaboration. MicroPort plans vascular electrode/delivery hardware; OYMotion plans decoding and rehabilitation robotics. Clinical studies are prospective in the agreement.

companyDossiers.name: Brain Navi Biotechnology

origin.detail: Jerry Chen founded Brain Navi in Taiwan in 2015. His official conference biography records participation in the Stanford–Taiwan Biomedical Program in 2012, a medical-device innovation-training link.

precursor.detail: NaoTrac’s technical basis combines image registration, machine vision and robotic instrument positioning. A specific academic precursor or licensed university invention was not verified.

companyChanges.detail: The company brought the navigation system from an early human procedure into a cleared stereotaxic guidance product. It supports electrode placement among other surgical tasks, which makes it enabling surgical infrastructure for neurotechnology.
